summary: Geopolitical alerts that can move oil. Scans every 10 minutes in the morning, every 5 minutes from noon to 10:00 pm, every 10 minutes late evening and every hour overnight (2:00 am to 8:00 am Singapore time) on weekdays, and every 3 hours from Saturday 3:00 am to Monday 3:00 am Singapore time. Counts and the net read cover the rolling last 24 hours; the feed lists all stored alerts.

netRead.bottom: Attacks on Hormuz shipping and Saudi oil sites, an IRGC threat to shut the southern corridor and a US cold snap keep risks tilted higher.

alerts.headline: Iran reportedly struck Oman's Didamar Island in southern Hormuz, with footage showing smoke over radar and communications gear; the IRGC claims it disabled the navigation system used by US Navy-assisted ships and threatens to shut all shipping on the southern corridor (may be the same strike as the navigation aids reported at 12:16 pm)
alerts.source: Open Source Intel, citing IRGC claims and footage

alerts.headline: Saudi Press Agency: Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline, the main route for bypassing Hormuz, was targeted in the Medina region on 9 Nov; a limited fire was put out with no injuries and no impact on operations

alerts.headline: Iran's Tasnim denies reports that security chief Mohsen Rezaei met US VP Vance in Doha; a senior Tehran official says no talks are planned until the US acts on Iran's seven conditions

alerts.headline: Turkish intelligence chief Kalın says Qatar will host US VP JD Vance and Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei in Doha next week to try to break the stalled US-Iran talks; Tehran has not confirmed

alerts.headline: Unconfirmed: UAE's Khor Fakkan closes Al Luluyah beach after an oil spill is spotted along the coast near the Gulf of Oman port; source of the spill not stated
alerts.source: First Squawk citing a local notice; also Giovanni Staunovo

alerts.headline: UKMTO reclassifies a 7 Nov incident near Khasab, Oman, as an attack: a tanker caught fire and its crew was evacuated (late report)

alerts.headline: Unconfirmed: Saudi airstrikes reportedly hit Hodeidah International Airport and the nearby town of Al-Eisi on Yemen's Red Sea coast, a new escalation after Houthi fire on Riyadh

alerts.headline: Unconfirmed: Iran has apparently dropped its demand to control the Strait of Hormuz and collect transit fees from passing ships, Israel Hayom reports; Brent dips below $96

alerts.headline: Unconfirmed: several explosions reported in the Strait of Hormuz, possibly IRGC Navy anti-ship missile launches; Iran's Fars says another oil tanker is ablaze after hitting a mine

alerts.headline: Rosneft reimposes fuel purchase limits at Russian filling stations (30 L in cities, 50 L on highways, diesel capped) after Ukrainian refinery strikes; Karelia, Zabaykalsky, Buryatia, Novosibirsk and others confirm

alerts.headline: Saudi Civil Defense issues a danger warning in Riyadh after a ballistic missile is reported launched from Yemen toward the capital; officials declared the danger over about two minutes later, no impact reported
alerts.source: Saudi Civil Defense (official) on the warning and the all-clear; AMK Mapping (OSINT) on the missile launch; First Squawk; no interception or impact reported

alerts.headline: Israel's Channel 13: CENTCOM's Adm. Cooper told Israeli military leaders to prepare for a possible third wave of US strikes on Iran, which could extend to bridges, power stations and energy infrastructure

dayNote.title: Today's key developments
lines: Saudi Arabia says its East-West pipeline, the main Hormuz bypass, was targeted near Medina, and Iran reportedly hit radar on Oman's Didamar Island in southern Hormuz.
The IRGC now threatens to shut the southern shipping corridor, Tehran rules out US talks until its seven conditions are met, and a US cold snap looms.
